passage: Friday, early March: Keerthana spent her free evening in bed with her phone, thumb moving for hours. She went to sleep somehow more tired, jaw tight. Saturday, a week later: her friend Yamini dragged her to a pottery class above the bakery. Keerthana's hands were caked in clay, the wheel wobbled, and she forgot to check anything for two whole hours. Walking home, she noticed her shoulders had dropped. That night she made a list: pottery, walks by the sea, dinners with Yamini, plain quiet with the window open. Late April: Keerthana's work calendar had a block every Saturday afternoon marked 'maintenance'. When her manager asked for a weekend call, she offered Monday instead.

qa.q: Where was the pottery class?
qa.a: Above the bakery.

qa.q: How did Keerthana feel after the evening on her phone?
qa.a: She felt more tired and tense, jaw tight, as if the scrolling had not rested her at all.

qa.q: What did Keerthana do to protect the rest that worked?
qa.a: She listed what really refreshed her and blocked Saturday afternoons as 'maintenance', offering Monday instead of a weekend call.

qa.q: What might Yamini have noticed about Keerthana after the pottery class?
qa.a: Yamini may have seen a looser, lighter friend with dropped shoulders, compared with the tense one Yamini had dragged along.

grounding: Shows a person discovering that pottery, walks, friends and quiet refresh her more than scrolling, and protecting that time each week as maintenance rather than a reward.

passage: Sumit, you asked how I lasted thirty years on the wards. I'll tell you. At twenty-four I was a young nurse in Goa: work, then collapse in front of the television, then work again. I thought rest was a treat you had to earn. I snapped at patients' families. One evening my friend Lourdes, from the same ward, said, 'Maria, when did you last swim?' I had loved the sea as a girl. That Sunday I swam at dawn and came back hungry and laughing. So I made a rule: Tuesday and Sunday mornings, the sea, whatever happened. Some weeks the matron grumbled. I went anyway, the way you oil a machine. I was a kinder nurse for it. Now tell me, Sumit, what is your sea?

qa.q: What did young Maria do at twenty-four?
qa.a: Maria worked as a young nurse in Goa.

qa.q: How did young Maria feel after swimming at dawn that Sunday?
qa.a: Maria felt refreshed and happy, coming back hungry and laughing.

qa.q: What choice turned things around for young Maria?
qa.a: Making a rule to swim on Tuesday and Sunday mornings whatever happened, treating it as upkeep rather than a treat to be earned.

qa.q: How might Lourdes have seen Maria before that Sunday swim?
qa.a: Lourdes probably saw a worn-out friend who snapped at families and had lost touch with what Maria loved, which is why Lourdes asked about swimming.

grounding: Shows, through an elder's memory, a person discovering that the sea, not television, truly refreshed Maria, and protecting that time each week as maintenance rather than a reward.

passage: Nazia had worked out that scrolling left her more tired, while her Wednesday evening walk round the lake left her light. So she guarded it like a meeting: no calls after six. This Wednesday the monsoon crashed down and the lake path flooded. Her thumb drifted to the video app out of habit. After five minutes she caught herself, feeling the familiar dull buzz. Instead she texted Payal: 'Rain cancelled the lake. Chai and carrom at mine?' Payal came over with wet hair and pakoras. They played three games, laughing at every bad shot. Nazia went to bed rested, not drained, and wrote next Wednesday's walk into her diary again.

qa.q: What did Nazia text Payal?
qa.a: 'Rain cancelled the lake. Chai and carrom at mine?'

qa.q: How did Nazia feel after five minutes of scrolling?
qa.a: She felt a familiar dull, drained buzz, a sign that scrolling was not restoring her.

qa.q: Which choice kept Nazia's evening restful?
qa.a: She swapped the walk for chai and carrom with a friend instead of scrolling, protecting the evening.

qa.q: What is it like for Payal to be invited over on a rainy Wednesday?
qa.a: Payal probably felt pleased to be included, arriving with pakoras and sharing the laughter.

grounding: A young woman protects the rest that truly refreshes her, even when rain cancels her walk.

passage: By Friday night Jagdish usually lay on the sofa for hours flicking through videos, and woke on Saturday feeling foggy. One week he tried an experiment and noted how he felt after each thing. Scrolling: heavy. Watering the terrace plants: calm. Half an hour of tabla: bright. Sunday morning cricket with his colleague Siddharth's building team: tired but happy. Now the tabla has a fixed slot on Tuesday and Friday evenings, and he says no to late office calls then. When Siddharth teased, 'So rest is your prize for good behaviour?' Jagdish said, 'No, it's servicing, like the scooter. Skip it and it costs more later.'

qa.q: What fixed slots does the tabla have now?
qa.a: Tuesday and Friday evenings.

qa.q: Why did Jagdish start noting how he felt after each activity?
qa.a: He felt foggy and heavy after long scrolling and was curious which activities truly left him calm or bright.

qa.q: What does Jagdish mean by calling rest servicing?
qa.a: Like servicing a scooter, regular restoring time keeps him running well, and skipping it costs more later.

qa.q: How might Siddharth see Jagdish's fixed tabla slots?
qa.a: Siddharth teases that rest is a prize, but may come to see it as a sensible habit.

grounding: A young man notices which activities truly refresh him and protects them in his week as upkeep.

passage:
'Uday, Mausi is coming Saturday morning. Can you skip your cycling?'
'Leela, can she come at eleven instead? I'll be back by ten.'
'It's just one ride.'
'Remember the month I skipped it? I was snapping at you by Wednesday.'
'True. You were horrible.' She laughed.
'Those two hours by the river keep me sane. It isn't a treat, it's like brushing my teeth.'
'Fine. Eleven. But then you make the tea for Mausi.'
'Deal. And what about you? What fills you up?'
'Honestly? Singing. I haven't sung since the wedding.'
'Then Sunday mornings are yours. I'll handle the phone.'

qa.q: What time did Uday suggest Mausi come?
qa.a: At eleven.

qa.q: Why does Uday want to keep the Saturday ride?
qa.a: Uday feels steadier after it and remembers feeling irritable and snappy the month it was skipped.

qa.q: What arrangement did Uday and Leela reach?
qa.a: Mausi comes at eleven after the ride, Uday makes the tea, and Sunday mornings become Leela's time for singing.

qa.q: What might Leela realise when asked what fills her up?
qa.a: Leela realises she has not sung since the wedding and may feel touched that Uday wants to protect her rest too.

grounding: A couple protect the activities that truly restore them as regular upkeep, not rewards.

passage: For most of last year, my "rest" was lying on the sofa scrolling until midnight, and I'd wake up on Monday feeling like I'd never had a weekend. I'm Madhuri, and I finally tried an experiment. For a month I jotted down after each free evening how I felt: heavier or lighter? Scrolling: heavier, every time. What made me lighter surprised me. Tuesday pottery class with Gurpreet, even when I botched the bowl. A long walk to the flower market on Saturday morning. Twenty minutes on the balcony doing absolutely nothing, just watching the neem tree. So I put those in my calendar like meetings: Tuesday clay, Saturday walk, balcony every evening. I don't wait to earn them anymore. It's maintenance, like oiling a cycle. My Mondays feel different now.

qa.q: What did Madhuri jot down after each free evening?
qa.a: How Madhuri felt: heavier or lighter.

qa.q: How did Madhuri feel after an evening of scrolling?
qa.a: Madhuri felt heavy and unrested, as if there had never been a weekend.

qa.q: Why does putting rest in the calendar help?
qa.a: It protects the activities that truly refresh Madhuri and treats them as maintenance, not a reward to be earned.

qa.q: How might Gurpreet experience Madhuri turning up every Tuesday?
qa.a: Gurpreet probably enjoys the steady company at pottery and may notice Madhuri seeming lighter.

grounding: Shows a person noticing that pottery, walks and plain quiet refresh far more than scrolling, and protecting them in the week as maintenance rather than reward.
